newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India GDRs slip on oil price fears.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India GDRs slip on oil price fears.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts were lower on Tuesday despite gains in Bombay as investors digest earnings news and seek cover from anticipated hikes in petroleum prices, traders said.
They said prices were likely to be capped in the near term in sectors that would be hurt by a petroleum rise. "Chemicals and cement would suffer from a knock-on effect," a trader said.
But Indian global depository receipt were also seen hurt by investor sentiment pushing assets towards other markets, traders said.
"People see London and Wall Street on new highs and think - why mess around in India for a marginal return?" said a trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 0.52 points down at 77.74, with the premium over the local market at 18.49 percent versus 17.86 percent.

Term lending institution Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) added 87 cents at $10.50/$11.00 as London investors reacted to a 62 percent jump in earnings announced Monday. Bajaj Auto shed $1.10 at $30.50/$32.00.
Taiwanese GDRs rose in line with gains in Taipei, where a recent bull run continued despite late profit taking.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index added 2.39 points, or 2.02 percent, to 121.05, representing a discount to the local market of 2.85 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index lost 0.69 points to 61.57 points, a premium of 30.37 percent over the local market.
